hints.content:
The measure of an arc is equal to the measure of the [[☃ definition 1]] that intercepts it.

By that reasoning, the arc measure of minor arc $\stackrel{\large{\frown}}{CD}$ is the acute measure of $\angle CPD$.  We need to find the measure of  major arc $\stackrel{\large{\frown}}{CAD}$, which is the [[☃ definition 2]] of minor arc $\stackrel{\large{\frown}}{CD}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

hints.content:
From the diagram, we see that $\angle APE$ and $\angle EPD$ are supplementary.  The measures of supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$.  Thus:

$\begin{align}
m\angle APE + m\angle EPD&=180
\\\\
90 + (33k-9)  &= 180
\\\\
81+ 33k &= 180
\\\\
33k &= 99
\\\\
k &= 3
\end{align}$.

We can use the value of $k$ to evaluate the measure of $\angle CPD$.  Let's substitute in our value for $k$.

$\begin{align}
m\angle CPD&= 20k+4^\circ
\\\\
&=20(3)+4^\circ
\\\\
&=60+4^\circ
\\\\
&=64^\circ
\end{align}$

There are $360^\circ$ in a circle, so the measure of any major arc is equal to $360^\circ$ minus the measure of the corresponding minor arc.

$m\stackrel{\large{\frown}}{CAD} \,= 360^\circ-64^\circ$
